newsitem.title: CANADA: CAI crisis misunderstood by minister - union.
newsitem.headline: CAI crisis misunderstood by minister - union.

text.p: Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson's refusal to re-regulate the airline industry shows he does not understand Canadian Airlines Corp's financial crisis, a union leader said on Monday.
Anderson in a speech in Montreal on Monday ruled out restricting domestic air routes and blocking new entrants into the industry.

Both concepts are main bargaining points for the 5,300-member International Association of Machinists and 3,700-member Canadian Auto workers, as they propose alternatives to a 10-percent employee wage cut outlined in the company's survival plan.
"The minister's statement shows an incredible lack of knowldge of what's happening in this industry and to what we're calling for," said CAW president Buzz Hargrove.
Hargrove said the CAW has not proposed shutting down new discount carriers, as Anderson suggested in his speech.
CAW and IAM officials contend that employee wages were not the cause of Canadian's current financial problem, so should not be part of the solution.

The wage cuts are part of a three-pronged plan to rescue the ailing airline. Other initiatives include major route restructurings and a C$48-million annual cut to service fees paid to AMR Corp, parent of American Airlines.
Union officials were meeting in Vancouver on Monday with union negotiators to hammer out an agreement on the plan and alternatives discussed last week. The factions were set to meet again on Tuesday.
Hargrove said, however, that Anderson has so far not responded to requests to meet with the union to discuss its own alternatives to Canadian's life-support strategy.

"He hasn't had the courtesy to meet with us," Hargrove said. "We sent him a letter. I sent the prime minister another letter today asking for a meeting to explain our case, because they obviously don't understand it."

Also on Monday, frustration with the ruling Liberal Party's inaction on the Canadian crisis sparked demonstrations by employees in front of the offices of members of parliament in Toronto and Vancouver.
After his speech in Montreal, Anderson told reporters he believed Canadian would not be forced into bankruptcy because the management plan would work. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
